newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to further probe French textiles aid plan.
newsitem.headline: EU to further probe French textiles aid plan.

text.p: The European Commission is expected to extend a probe on Wednesday into a controversial French government plan to help its textile industry, Commission sources said on Tuesday.

The Commission openly questioned in May a 2.1-billion-franc ($408 million) proposal to reduce salary-linked contributions paid by textile, clothing and leather industries in France in order to stimulate job creation.
While encouraging measures to boost employment, the Commission warned at the time that the French plan could distort competition in the European Union's market.

But France has counter-attacked saying the help is necessary to compensate for collective agreements in the sectors concerned which translate into a reduction in working hours without equivalent pay cuts, the sources said.

"Is it the role of the state to compensate for companies' increased costs due to collective agreements?" a Commission official asked, leaving little doubt that the EU executive was close to saying it should not be the case.

The Commission has consistently rejected other national attempts in the recent past to help specific industries resist international competition. It particularly outlawed similar measures for the Italian shoe industry and Belgian export-led firms.

It has encouraged instead a general, across the board, reduction of contributions to social security schemes as a way to reduce the bloc's huge unemployment. -- Amelia Torres 322 2876841 ($ = 5.150 French Francs)
